insights.headline: Softer US inflation cools October Fed-hike bets; gold steadies near $4,210 after a brutal September
insights.summary: Gold bounced to $4,213 an ounce on Wednesday after August core PCE came in cooler than expected at 3.0%, pushing October Fed-hike odds below 35%. The rebound barely dents a bruising month: spot gold fell 8.5% and silver 13.5% in September as real yields re-priced at the fastest pace in four years. For Indian buyers, a rebounding rupee and steady MCX prices near ₹1.50 lakh offer some relief ahead of the festive season, while high taxes push more purchases off the books.
points: Gold +0.7% to $4,213 on cooler August core PCE (3.0% vs 3.3% expected); October hike odds below 35%.
September: spot gold -8.5%, silver -13.5%; real 10-year TIPS yields jumped at the fastest pace in 4 years.
Rupee rebounds to 95.83 vs dollar as crude eases; stable in H1 FY27 after a 10% FY26 fall.
US gold ETFs drew $3.8B in September; China's central bank bought 20+ tons in August, its 22nd straight month.
September NFP report due Friday — the next test for Fed policy bets.

trending.title: October Fed-hike bets collapse on softer PCE
trending.summary: Core PCE at 3.0% and a 2.2% Q2 GDP beat sent gold to $4,213 and cut October hike odds from 70% to under 35% — but the 10-year still hit 5.30%.

trending.title: A brutal September for bullion
trending.summary: Spot gold lost 8.5% and silver 13.5% as real yields re-priced at the fastest pace in four years; December futures logged gold's worst month since June.

trending.title: Rupee relief cushions MCX buyers
trending.summary: The rupee rebounded to 95.83 as crude eased and stayed stable through H1 FY27 after a 10% FY26 slide — a softer currency cushion with gold near ₹1.50 lakh.

trending.title: Tax bite pushes gold off the books
trending.summary: With import duty at 15% plus 3% GST, more Indian buyers are paying cash without receipts to save up to 6% — a grey-market side effect of the duty hike.

trending.title: Silver holds the $60 line
trending.summary: Silver touched $61.50 on the inflation data but faces fresh selling risk near $61; Morgan Stanley says its earlier run to $120 was driven by fundamentals, not hype.

items.title: Softer August PCE (core 3.0%) and 2.2% Q2 GDP send gold to session highs near $4,213
items.summary: Spot gold jumped 0.74% to $4,213.11 an ounce on Wednesday after the BEA said annual core PCE was 3.0% in August, cooler than the 3.3% consensus, with headline inflation at 3.4% against 3.7% expected. Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2%. BullionVault notes betting on an October Fed hike fell below 35% on the news.

items.title: Gold down 8.5% and silver 13.5% in September as real yields re-price at the fastest pace in four years
items.summary: Gold and silver closed out a bruising September down 8.5% and 13.5% respectively, despite a Wednesday spike to $4,218 and $61.50 on softer US inflation data that erased itself within hours. Inflation-protected US Treasury yields jumped the fastest in four years, adding 0.44 points to the real 10-year rate close to a record high. September's nonfarm payrolls report is due Friday.

items.title: Gold retreats as 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.30%; $4,160–$4,180 support in focus
items.summary: Gold failed to hold $4,200 on Wednesday and pulled back as the US 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.30%, keeping pressure on non-yielding bullion. October Fed-hike odds eased to 39.3% as crude prices softened, but yields kept climbing. FXEmpire flags $4,160–$4,180 as near-term support, with $4,300–$4,320 resistance above.

items.title: Morgan Stanley's Gower sees gold back above $5,000 in H2 2027; silver's run to $120 driven by more than hype
items.summary: Morgan Stanley's Amy Gower told CNBC she expects gold to trade back above $5,000 an ounce within a year, citing strong ETF and central-bank demand despite 20-year-high long-dated yields and dollar strength. She said silver's surge to $120 was driven by fundamentals rather than hype, and pointed to China's record gold imports and Golden Week buying as support.

items.title: Gold's worst month since June: the safe-haven playbook breaks down as yields win
items.summary: December gold futures fell 6.6% in September to $4,186.70, the worst month since June, even as oil spiked and inflation fears returned — because climbing Treasury yields and a dollar up over 2% in September raised gold's opportunity cost. Countering the gloom: US gold ETFs drew $3.8 billion in September and China's central bank bought over 20 tons in August, its 22nd straight month of buying.

items.title: Rupee rebounds to 95.83 against the dollar as crude prices ease
items.summary: The rupee strengthened to 95.83 per dollar as easing crude prices and likely central-bank support pulled it back from an intraday low of 96.15. A firmer rupee lowers the landed cost of imported gold and silver, cushioning MCX prices for Indian buyers.

items.title: Rupee relatively stable in H1 FY27 after 10% fall in FY26
items.summary: Business Standard reports the rupee was relatively stable in the first half of FY27 after falling about 10% in FY26. Currency stability matters for bullion buyers: the rupee's slide earlier in the year amplified the global gold rally for Indian shoppers.

items.title: High gold prices and steep taxes push more Indian buyers toward off-the-books cash deals
items.summary: Mint reports that soaring gold prices and the import duty hike to 15% (plus 3% GST) are driving more buyers into under-the-counter cash sales without invoices, where bulk buyers can save up to 6%. The shift toward the grey market ahead of the wedding season is an unintended consequence of the policy meant to curb bullion purchases and protect forex reserves.

items.title: Gold at 7-week low: September 30 outlook maps support and resistance
items.summary: Gold is at a seven-week low near $4,178 spot (Rs 1,49,940 on MCX) with the bias cautious as yields and Fed policy dominate. Support: $4,100/$4,025 (Rs 1,47,100/Rs 1,44,500 on MCX); resistance $4,300/$4,380. Silver CMP is $61 ($2,26,100 on MCX); support $59/$57, resistance $63.50/$65.50. The PCE print and Friday's payrolls will set October Fed odds; China's Oct 1-7 Golden Week may lift demand.

items.title: MCX bullion steadies after sharp correction; 24K gold Rs 1,49,570
items.summary: Domestic bullion steadied after a sharp correction: 24K gold was at Rs 1,49,570 per 10g (+0.52%), 22K at Rs 1,37,100, 18K at Rs 1,12,180, and silver at Rs 2,26,190 a kg. Global cues, a weaker rupee and pre-festive buying cushioned the downside. Gold support at Rs 1,45,500-1,46,800, resistance at Rs 1,52,000; silver support at Rs 2,24,500, resistance at Rs 2,32,000. Add 3% GST to quoted prices.

items.title: Silver eyes $61 as recovery meets fresh selling risk
items.summary: Silver fell to $60.30 on Tuesday, its lowest level since August 5, with RSI at 28 signaling oversold conditions though that alone does not guarantee a bounce. Resistance is set at $61, then $61.80-85 and $62.40-45; support sits at $60, $59.35-40 and $56.55-60. Traders need sustained buying to overcome resistance as the downtrend remains intact.

items.title: Why the 30-year Treasury's 2002-high yield matters for Indian markets
items.summary: The US 30-year crossed 5.6%, its highest since June 2002, while the 10-year hit 5.214% -- driven by Fed rate expectations, oil-driven inflation risk, heavy borrowing and AI-led capital demand. For India: elevated US yields pull foreign investors toward US fixed income, pressuring the Sensex and Nifty, while a weaker rupee erodes dollar returns -- a loop that can weigh on both.
